title: Why Every Organism Needs One Name
subject: Biology
objective: Aam, mango, maamidi: one fruit, many names, and one word robin for two different birds. With about 1.8 million species, science needs one name per organism.

fill.q: About 1.7 to 1.8 ____ species have been described.
The scientific name of mango is Mangifera ____.
Giving standard names to organisms is called ____.
Aam and mango are ____ names of one fruit.
A scientific name belongs to only ____ organism.

tf.q: A scientific name is the same all over the world.
Local names are the same everywhere.
tf.explain: They change from place to place.

tf.q: "Robin" means the same species in Europe and America.
One organism has one scientific name.

ar.a: Scientists need a standard name for each organism.
ar.r: Local names differ from place to place.

ar.a: One common name can cover different species.
ar.r: "Robin" names different birds in Europe and America.

mcq.explain: The American robin is Turdus migratorius.

mcq.q: Local names are a problem because they:

short.q: Give two reasons why local names are not enough for science.
short.solution: They vary from place to place, and one name can mean different organisms.

short.q: What two properties must a scientific name have?
short.solution: It is the same worldwide, and it belongs to only one organism.

match.explain: Each local name matches its language.
